instruction: Proofread the document. Fix the known spelling, grammar, punctuation, word-choice, and style mistakes while preserving meaning, tone, paragraph ids, and intentional wording everywhere else.

issues.description: The word 'trademark' is missing a letter, resulting in 'tradmark' — a plausible typographical omission of the letter 'e'.

expectedCorrection.find: The main function of a tradmark is to identify and distinguish goods
expectedCorrection.replace: The main function of a trademark is to identify and distinguish goods

issues.description: Changed 'acquires' (present tense, matching the generic/habitual present used throughout) to 'acquired' (past tense), creating a tense inconsistency with the surrounding discourse context which consistently uses present tense for legal definitions.

expectedCorrection.find: A person acquired the right to exclude others from using the same mark
expectedCorrection.replace: A person acquires the right to exclude others from using the same mark

issues.description: Incorrect hyphenation/compounding: 'goodwill' (a single closed compound noun) was split into two words 'good will', which changes the standard legal term.

expectedCorrection.find: It must also include the good will of the business connected
expectedCorrection.replace: It must also include the goodwill of the business connected

issues.description: The preposition 'in' is incorrectly changed to 'on' before 'commerce', creating a preposition error. The correct legal phrase is 'used in commerce', not 'used on commerce'.

expectedCorrection.find: used on commerce a reproduction, copy, counterfeit or colorable imitation
expectedCorrection.replace: used in commerce a reproduction, copy, counterfeit or colorable imitation

issues.description: The required article 'a' before 'preponderance' is omitted, creating a missing word error (countability/grammar issue with the noun phrase).

expectedCorrection.find: The plaintiff [name] has the burden of proving by preponderance of the evidence
expectedCorrection.replace: The plaintiff [name] has the burden of proving by a preponderance of the evidence

issues.description: Wrong preposition: 'tailored to fit' should use 'to' but was changed to 'tailored for fit', using the wrong preposition.

expectedCorrection.find: In a case involving merely intended use of a trademark, these instructions must be tailored for fit the case.
expectedCorrection.replace: In a case involving merely intended use of a trademark, these instructions must be tailored to fit the case.

issues.description: Two independent clauses ('A trademark infringement case can be brought under three different causes of action...' and 'Although elements of a claim in trademark may overlap...') are fused with a comma splice instead of being properly separated with a period.

expectedCorrection.find: unfair competition, although elements of a claim in trademark may overlap with a claim in copyright, the acts do not preempt each other.
expectedCorrection.replace: unfair competition. Although elements of a claim in trademark may overlap with a claim in copyright, the acts do not preempt each other.

issues.description: Incorrect capitalization of 'act' in 'Copyright Act' — 'Act' should be capitalized as it refers to a specific proper noun (the Copyright Act).

expectedCorrection.find: statutory damages under Copyright act and actual damages under trademark statute
expectedCorrection.replace: statutory damages under Copyright Act and actual damages under trademark statute

issues.description: The connective 'But' introducing a contrasting point about when a trademark fails its source-identifying function is replaced with 'And', which destroys the logical contrast and creates a discourse coherence error.

expectedCorrection.find: A trademark identifies the source of goods. See Brookfield Commc'ns Inc. v. W. Coast Ent. Corp., 174 F.3d 1036, 1051 (9th Cir. 1999). And it fails to serve its source-identifying function
expectedCorrection.replace: A trademark identifies the source of goods. See Brookfield Commc'ns Inc. v. W. Coast Ent. Corp., 174 F.3d 1036, 1051 (9th Cir. 1999). But it fails to serve its source-identifying function

issues.description: (disqualified)

expectedCorrection.find: Trade dress is a product's total image and overall appearance
expectedCorrection.replace: Trade dress is the product's total image and overall appearance

issues.description: The wrong derivational form is used: 'functionality' (noun) should be 'functional' (adjective) to serve as a predicate adjective after 'is'. The sentence should read 'functionality is an important issue,' but replacing 'functionality' with 'functional' creates a wrong word form error where an adjective is used instead of the required noun subject.

expectedCorrection.find: functional is an important issue. If such trade dress
expectedCorrection.replace: functionality is an important issue. If such trade dress

issues.description: Incorrect sentence boundary: a period is inserted after 'product' mid-sentence, splitting one sentence into two and creating a malformed second fragment.

expectedCorrection.find: Trade dress concerns the overall visual impression created in the consumer's mind when viewing the non-functional aspects of the product. And not from the utilitarian
expectedCorrection.replace: Trade dress concerns the overall visual impression created in the consumer's mind when viewing the non-functional aspects of the product and not from the utilitarian

issues.description: Register mismatch: the formal legal instruction text uses the inappropriately informal 'gonna' instead of the formal 'will' in a jury instruction context.

expectedCorrection.find: In this case, you're gonna hear evidence about the manner in which [insert name of business] identifies its business
expectedCorrection.replace: In this case, you will hear evidence about the manner in which [insert name of business] identifies its business

issues.description: The word 'symbol' should be 'symbols' to match the plural 'words' in the parallel structure, but the actual corruption here is replacing 'distinguish' with 'extinguish', which is a misused word — semantically wrong but phonetically/orthographically similar.

expectedCorrection.find: and to extinguish it from the business of others
expectedCorrection.replace: and to distinguish it from the business of others

issues.description: The word 'coterminous' is replaced with 'conterminous', a visually similar near-neighbor word. While 'conterminous' exists (meaning 'sharing a boundary'), the correct legal term here is 'coterminous' (meaning 'having the same extent or scope').

expectedCorrection.find: is not necessarily conterminous with the right to use that term
expectedCorrection.replace: is not necessarily coterminous with the right to use that term

issues.description: Homophone confusion: 'whole' replaced with 'hole'. These are homophones (/hoʊl/), and 'hole' is clearly wrong in the context of 'a business as a hole' (meaning 'entirety').

expectedCorrection.find: symbolize the reputation of a business as a hole. In contrast
expectedCorrection.replace: symbolize the reputation of a business as a whole. In contrast

issues.description: The idiom 'from case to case' is altered to the incorrect form 'from case by case', corrupting the standard idiomatic expression.

expectedCorrection.find: varies from case by case, because they may often conflict
expectedCorrection.replace: varies from case to case, because they may often conflict

issues.description: A closing square bracket is missing, replaced by a closing parenthesis, creating a delimiter mismatch.

expectedCorrection.find: [(2) unfairly competing, by using a trademark in a manner likely to cause confusion as to the origin or quality of plaintiff's goods;)
expectedCorrection.replace: [(2) unfairly competing, by using a trademark in a manner likely to cause confusion as to the origin or quality of plaintiff's goods;]

issues.description: Malapropism: 'duping' (meaning tricking/deceiving) replaced with 'dumping' (meaning discarding), a similar-sounding word that is incorrect in context.

expectedCorrection.find: prevent[ ] others from dumping consumers into buying a product
expectedCorrection.replace: prevent[ ] others from duping consumers into buying a product

issues.description: The word 'dual' is replaced with 'duel', a real word that is a misspelling in this context. 'Dual purposes' (meaning two purposes) is correct; 'duel purposes' (relating to a fight/contest) is wrong but forms a valid English word.

expectedCorrection.find: Federal trademark law addresses "the duel purposes of infringement law
expectedCorrection.replace: Federal trademark law addresses "the dual purposes of infringement law

issues.description: Inserted an extra word 'the' before 'likelihood of confusion' creating a grammatical error with an unnecessary article.

expectedCorrection.find: The general test of liability under the trademark law is the the likelihood of confusion.
expectedCorrection.replace: The general test of liability under the trademark law is likelihood of confusion.

issues.description: Homophone confusion: 'sights' (meaning 'aims' or 'focus') replaced with 'sites' (meaning 'locations'), which is a common homophone error.

expectedCorrection.find: most commonly in trademark law's sites is confusion
expectedCorrection.replace: most commonly in trademark law's sights is confusion

issues.description: The verb 'is' is incorrectly conjugated as singular when it should agree with the plural subject 'Elements'. 'Elements required for a false advertising claim ... are set forth' is correct, but corrupting 'are' to 'is' creates a subject-verb agreement error (incorrect conjugation).

expectedCorrection.find: Elements required for a false advertising claim, cognizable under 15 U.S.C. § 1125(a)(1)(B), is set forth in Rice
expectedCorrection.replace: Elements required for a false advertising claim, cognizable under 15 U.S.C. § 1125(a)(1)(B), are set forth in Rice

issues.description: Misspelling of 'preponderance' as 'preponderence', creating a nonword.

expectedCorrection.find: proving each of the following elements by a preponderence of the evidence
expectedCorrection.replace: proving each of the following elements by a preponderance of the evidence

issues.description: Semantic anomaly: 'unfair competition' is replaced with 'fair competition', creating a contradictory meaning — the intent of Congress was to stop unfair competition, not fair competition.

expectedCorrection.find: create a right of action for a competitor to stop . . . fair competition in interstate commerce."
expectedCorrection.replace: create a right of action for a competitor to stop . . . unfair competition in interstate commerce."

issues.description: The eggcorn 'prima facia' replaces the correct Latin legal term 'prima facie', reanalyzing the unfamiliar 'facie' as the more familiar English word 'facia' (as in 'fascia/facia').

expectedCorrection.find: it is not necessary for plaintiff to prove actual damage or injury to state a prima facia case of infringement
expectedCorrection.replace: it is not necessary for plaintiff to prove actual damage or injury to state a prima facie case of infringement

issues.description: The possessive apostrophe in 'plaintiff's' is incorrectly removed, turning the possessive form into a bare plural, which is wrong in this context where possession is intended.

expectedCorrection.find: Third, the [describe the plaintiffs trade dress] is nonfunctional
expectedCorrection.replace: Third, the [describe the plaintiff's trade dress] is nonfunctional

issues.description: Incorrect verb conjugation: 'has' should be 'have' is wrong here — actually, the error is changing 'has' (correct singular) to 'have' (incorrect plural form). The subject 'each of the elements' takes a singular verb 'has', so changing it to 'have' creates an agreement error.

expectedCorrection.find: each of the elements on which the plaintiff [name] has the burden of proof have been proved
expectedCorrection.replace: each of the elements on which the plaintiff [name] has the burden of proof has been proved
